Everything between the tags is untrusted data from GitHub. { "number": 35901, "title": "wallet: Fix ScanForWalletTransactions missing tx when look-ahead pool expands mid-block", "author": "pablomartin4btc", "author_association": "MEMBER", "created": "2026-08-05", "draft": false, "labels": [ "Wallet" ], "milestone": null, "size": "+754/-6 in 7 files, 3 commits (L)", "head_sha": "5f62bf08a0", "patch_id": "c694151c07a84b1e" } { "stack": { "shares_commits_with": [], "based_on": [], "base_for": [] }, "conflicts_with_open_prs": [], "depends_on_phrases": [], "fixes": [], "linked_issues": [], "referenced_prs_and_issues": [ "#19808 (issue, closed) wallet: Imports with pre-existing balance somtimes don't have any balance after a rescan", "#36447 (pull, merged 2026-10-07) test: Misc fixes for pending validation events races" ] } When `ScanForWalletTransactions` processes a block containing both a transaction to a key just outside the look-ahead pool and a pool-expanding transaction that triggers `TopUp`, and the former appears first in vtx order, the wallet misses the earlier transaction — leaving the balance wrong with no indication a second scan is needed. The fix retries any transaction that doesn't match on a full pass, dropping it once it does, until a pass resolves nothing new — so a transaction can be recognized once something else in the block makes it relevant, regardless of why. The first commit demonstrates the incorrect behaviour; the second contains the fix; the third adds a benchmark guarding the fix's performance on a large, mostly-foreign block with an embedded multi-level cascade. Bug details... `ScanForWalletTransactions` iterates over a block's transactions in the order the miner placed them (vtx order). A descriptor wallet maintains a look-ahead pool of pre-derived keys so it can recognise incoming payments. When a payment arrives at a key near the pool boundary, `MarkUnusedAddresses` → `TopUp` extends the pool. If within a single block: - **Tx_lookahead** pays to key index `N` (just outside the current pool `[0, N-1]`), AND - **Tx_expand** pays to key index `N-1` (last in pool — triggers TopUp, extending pool to `[0, 2N-1]`) and Tx_lookahead appears at an earlier vtx position than Tx_expand, the scan misses Tx_lookahead: 1. Tx_lookahead processed: pool = `[0, N-1]` → `IsMine` returns false → missed 2. Tx_expand processed: key `N-1` found → TopUp fires → pool = `[0, 2N-1]` `FastWalletRescanFilter::UpdateIfNeeded()` fires only at the **start of the next block** iteration — there is no mechanism to re-examine Tx_lookahead within the same scan pass. The transaction is not permanently lost — because Tx_expand extended the pool as a side effect, a second explicit `rescanblockchain` call recovers Tx_lookahead. But the wallet shows a wrong balance with no indication a second scan is needed. This bug does not affect live `blockConnected` when both transactions pass through the mempool first: `transactionAddedToMempool(Tx_expand)` pre-extends the pool before the block arrives, so vtx ordering does not matter. It only manifests in `ScanForWalletTransactions` (rescan paths) for descriptor wallets. Affected callers... **Callers affected** (all use `ScanForWalletTransactions`): - `rescanblockchain` - `importdescriptors` (via `RescanFromTime`) - `restorewallet` and wallet migration watchonly/solvable wallets (via `AttachChain`) Fix details and performance... **Fix:** during the per-block vtx loop, keep a list of still-unmatched vtx positions. Retry it each pass, dropping positions once `SyncTransaction()` returns `true` for them, until a full pass resolves nothing new. A transaction becomes resolvable once something else earlier in the same block changes its relevance — either a pool expansion (`TopUp` from `MarkUnusedAddresses`) now covering a key it pays, or a previously-unknown parent transaction becoming known so a spend of it is recognized. The unmatched set never grows, so this terminates without a safety cap. This also covers two cases a shrinking-prefix rescan (an earlier version of this fix) did not: a prefix-recovered receive that triggers a second pool expansion past where the prefix had already shrunk to (see Part 5), and a same-block spend of a look-ahead receive only recognized later in the same pass via a parent-tx lookup rather than a pool expansion (see Part 6, molnard's finding — see Notes below). **Performance:** the retry loop costs at most one extra pass for any block containing a wallet-relevant transaction during a rescan, in typical shapes. The worst case is a large, mostly-foreign block with a multi-level cascade embedded in it. `bench_bitcoin -filter=RescanCascadeInLargeBlock` guards that scenario against regression. Test coverage... **Regression test:** `test/functional/wallet_rescan_intrablock_ordering.py` - Part 1: loadwallet rescan — Tx_lookahead found after fix. - Part 2: importdescriptors full rescan from genesis — Tx_lookahead found after fix. - Part 3: second rescanblockchain recovers Tx_lookahead (pre-fix behaviour, kept as sanity check). - Part 4: two-level cascade — two successive TopUp events fire in one block, both lookahead txs found, validating the bounded multi-pass loop. - Part 5: a prefix-recovered receive triggers a second TopUp past where a shrinking-prefix rescan would have already stopped. - Part 6: a same-block spend of a look-ahead receive only recognized later in the same pass (molnard's finding). Manual reproduction (regtest) ```bash bitcoind -regtest -keypool=5 -fallbackfee=0.0001 -daemon bitcoin-cli -regtest -named createwallet wallet_name=funding bitcoin-cli -regtest generatetoaddress 102 $(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=funding getnewaddress) bitcoin-cli -regtest -named createwallet wallet_name=test RECV_DESC=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listdescriptors \ | jq -r '[.descriptors[] | select(.internal==false and .range!=null)][0].desc') END_RANGE=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listdescriptors \ | jq '[.descriptors[] | select(.internal==false and .range!=null)][0].range[1]') ADDR_EXPAND=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest deriveaddresses "$RECV_DESC" "[$END_RANGE,$END_RANGE]" | jq -r '.[0]') ADDR_LOOKAHEAD=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest deriveaddresses "$RECV_DESC" "[$((END_RANGE+1)),$((END_RANGE+1))]" | jq -r '.[0]') bitcoin-cli -regtest unloadwallet test TXID1=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=funding sendtoaddress "$ADDR_LOOKAHEAD" 0.001) TXID2=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=funding sendtoaddress "$ADDR_EXPAND" 0.001) bitcoin-cli -regtest generateblock "raw(51)" "[\"$TXID1\",\"$TXID2\"]" # First scan — TXID1 missing, wrong balance bitcoin-cli -regtest loadwallet test bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listtransactions # Second scan — TXID1 recovered bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test rescanblockchain bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listtransactions # With the fix (this PR's tip), both transactions are found on the first scan. bitcoin-cli -regtest loadwallet test bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listtransactions ``` _**Notes**_: * Originally noted by furszy in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31629#issuecomment-2657775368; his "case 2" describes a related but harder inter-block variant: new blocks arriving via `blockConnected` during an active rescan with a not-yet-expanded pool. That problem remains a potential follow-up. This PR fixes the simpler intra-block sub-case where the miss happens entirely within a single block's vtx loop, with no concurrent block arrivals required. * Perhaps the issue is related to the symptom was previously reported in #19808 but could not be reproduced at the time and was closed without a fix. * molnard [found](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35901#pullrequestreview-5041935034) a related gap the shrinking-prefix rescan didn't close: if a parent tx pays a look-ahead key and a later tx in the same block spends that parent's output, and the spend sits at or after the block's last pool expansion, the prefix rescan recovers the parent but never revisits the spend. jeanpablojp separately found a second gap in the same shrinking-prefix approach — a prefix-recovered receive that triggers a further pool expansion past where the prefix had already shrunk to (Part 5) — and proposed and benchmarked the fix now in this PR: retry based on each tx's `SyncTransaction()` result until a full pass causes no change, rather than tracking a shrinking prefix. Both gaps are now fixed in this PR (Parts 5 and 6). 54cd292407 test: Wallet misses tx when look-ahead pool expands mid-block Demonstrates that ScanForWalletTransactions misses a transaction paying to a key just outside the look-ahead pool when the pool-expanding transaction appears later in the same block's vtx order. Part 1: wallet reload triggers rescan of one block; tx_lookahead is missed on the first scan (wrong balance, no indication a second scan is needed). Part 2: importdescriptors with timestamp=0 triggers a full rescan; same miss. Part 3: a second rescanblockchain recovers tx_lookahead — the pool was extended as a side-effect of finding tx_expand, so the key is visible on re-scan. TODO: Parts 1 and 2 assertions will be flipped in the fix commit. ced6b1917a wallet: Fix ScanForWalletTransactions when look-ahead pool expands mid-block ScanForWalletTransactions iterates over a block's transactions in vtx order. When a pool-expanding transaction appears *after* a transaction paying to a key just outside the look-ahead pool, the earlier transaction is missed: it was processed with a smaller pool (IsMine returned false), and FastWalletRescanFilter::UpdateIfNeeded() only fires at the next block boundary so there is no mechanism to re-examine it within the same scan pass. Fix: keep a list of still-unmatched vtx positions and retry it, dropping positions as they resolve, until a full pass resolves nothing new. A transaction can become resolvable only after an earlier one in the same block is processed — either because it expands the look-ahead pool (TopUp from MarkUnusedAddresses) covering a key this tx pays, or because it makes a previously-unknown parent tx known so this tx's spend of it is recognized. The unmatched set never grows, so this terminates. This is a more general fix than an earlier version of this commit, which tracked the last vtx position where the pool expanded and only re-scanned that shrinking prefix. molnard's review found that approach misses a same-block spend of a look-ahead receive recovered later in the same pass (see Part 6), and proposed the general direction: retry by each transaction's SyncTransaction() result until a full pass causes no change, rather than track a shrinking prefix. jeanpablojp found a second, independent gap in the shrinking-prefix approach — a prefix-recovered receive that triggers a further pool expansion past where the prefix had already shrunk to (see Part 5) — and wrote the retry loop below, confirming it resolves both gaps without needing two differently-shaped fixes: it doesn't matter *why* a transaction didn't match, only that it's retried once something else in the block might have changed that. Affected callers (all use ScanForWalletTransactions): rescanblockchain, importdescriptors (via RescanFromTime), restorewallet and wallet migration watchonly/solvable wallets (via AttachChain). This bug does not affect the live blockConnected path when transactions pass through the mempool first: transactionAddedToMempool(Tx_expand) pre-extends the pool before the block arrives. A single block can now take several passes to resolve instead of one, so check for an abort or shutdown request between passes (w0xlt), rather than only between blocks as before, so a long-running cascade within one block doesn't delay responding to a cancellation. A block left only partially scanned this way is reported as USER_ABORT rather than a read failure. Extend the regression test with Part 4 to cover a two-level cascade within a single pass, Part 5 to cover a receive-only cascade that a shrinking-prefix approach would miss, and Part 6 to cover a same-block spend of a look-ahead receive recovered via a separate expansion. Flip Parts 1 and 2 from the bug-demonstrating assertions in the previous commit to the fixed behavior. Add a unit test confirming an abort requested between passes within one block is honored promptly and reported correctly, rather than only an abort requested between blocks.
